thread:
Samir: Quickstart sample app failing for new users on README run. Steps: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples && cd quickstarts/node-onboard && npm install && node index.js -> Error: Missing API key. Can someone take a quick look?
Alisha: Can you paste the exact error output and which README command you used?
Samir: Here’s the output: 
```
Error: 401 Unauthorized: x-api-key header missing
    at Request.handleResponse (/app/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.js:45:23)
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)
```
I followed the README command under "Run locally": `export REDWOOD_KEY=... && node index.js`
Marco: Uh — that export looks suspicious. The runtime expects REDWOOD_API_KEY (we renamed env var last quarter). README still says REDWOOD_KEY.
Samir: Yup. Also noticed the example's import is `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` but the published v1.2.0 Node SDK now does a default export `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')`. So two bits of drift (env var + import).
Alisha: Oof. So two user-visible DX regressions from copy/paste. Thanks for catching.
docs-bot: :robot_face: docs-linter found 2 issues in /quickstarts/node-onboard/README.md: (1) env var name mismatch (should be REDWOOD_API_KEY), (2) Node SDK import style outdated. See lint report https://ci.internal.redwood/docs-lint/4567
Eve: I opened a small PR to fix both: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/1543 — changes README to use REDWOOD_API_KEY and updates the code snippet to the default export style.
Marco: Nice. Can you paste the fixed snippet here so I can eyeball?
Eve: Sure. Updated snippet: 
```javascript
// index.js (snippet)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

async function main() {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'hi' })
  console.log(res.text)
}
main()
```
Alisha: Looks good. Two follow-ups: 1) add a short note in the README about setting the env var (example `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...`), and 2) mention SDK retry parity — Node SDK currently ships with retries disabled by default, but the Python sample shows an exponential backoff example. We should be explicit so users aren't surprised.
Samir: Yep — I hit a separate flakiness where the first token request got a transient 502 and the example didn't retry. Had to re-run.
Marco: On the SDK side, we should align defaults. I'll file a tiny issue in the SDK repo to add a note and propose enabling a short retry envelope by default in Node (or at least in examples).
Eve: PR 1543 also adds a one-liner note about retries and links to the SDK docs. I'll extend it to include the exact env export example and a minimal retry wrapper snippet.
Alisha: Can we also add a CI integration test that runs the quickstart with a mocked backend so this kind of drift gets caught? A single `node index.js` run under CI with the env var set should be fast.
Marco: Agreed. I'll add a lightweight smoke test in examples/.github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml that runs for PRs touching quickstarts.
Samir: Thanks — that should stop future copy/paste rot. Also FYI: one user ran into this on the community Slack a few minutes ago. I'll post the PR link there when merged.
Alisha: Assigning tasks: @Eve finish README additions + merge PR, @Marco add smoke CI, @Alisha add a tiny test that asserts the sample prints a string. Anyone want to pick up backport to other languages (Python snippets) too?
Marco: I'll check Python snippets; likely the env var is fine there but I'll audit.
Samir: Great. Marking this resolved for now — will re-run quickstart after PR merges. :thumbsup:
